title.value: Amyloid-Related Imaging Abnormalities in 2 Phase 3 Studies Evaluating Aducanumab in Patients With Early Alzheimer Disease
title.quote: Amyloid-Related Imaging Abnormalities in 2 Phase 3 Studies Evaluating Aducanumab in Patients With Early Alzheimer Disease

design.value: Secondary analysis (pooled/integrated safety data set) of 2 double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 randomized clinical trials (EMERGE and ENGAGE)
design.quote: Secondary analysis of data from the EMERGE and ENGAGE trials, which were 2 double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3 randomized clinical trials that compared low-dose and high-dose aducanumab treatment with placebo among participants at 348 sites across 20 countries.

phase.quote: Following the PRIME trial, 2 identically designed global phase 3 trials, EMERGE and ENGAGE, assessed the safety and efficacy of aducanumab in patients with early AD.

n.quote: The combined studies consisted of a total of 3285 participants with Alzheimer disease who received 1 or more doses of placebo (n = 1087) or aducanumab (n = 2198; 2752 total person-years of exposure) during the placebo-controlled period.

n_description.value: The safety population: all participants who received at least 1 dose of study treatment (placebo or aducanumab) during the placebo-controlled period. ARIA analyses used the MRI safety population (n = 3253), those with at least 1 postbaseline MRI scan.
n_description.quote: The safety population (n = 3285) consisted of all participants who received at least 1 dose of study treatment (placebo or aducanumab) during the placebo-controlled period. ARIA analyses were based on the MRI safety population (n = 3253)

population.value: Individuals aged 50 to 85 years meeting clinical criteria for mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer disease or mild dementia due to Alzheimer disease, with amyloid pathology confirmed by visual assessment of amyloid PET; patients on nonaspirin antiplatelet agents or anticoagulation were excluded, as were patients with more than 4 microhemorrhages or any area of siderosis at baseline
population.quote: Trial participants were individuals aged 50 to 85 years who met clinical criteria for mild cognitive impairment due to AD or mild dementia due to AD, with amyloid pathology confirmed by visual assessment of amyloid positron emission tomography.

followup.value: Monthly intravenous doses over 76 weeks for a total of 20 doses (placebo-controlled period); postbaseline routine MRIs at weeks 14, 22, 30, 42, 54, 66, and 78
followup.quote: administered by monthly intravenous doses over 76 weeks for a total of 20 doses, and randomization was stratified by apolipoprotein E (ApoE) ε4 status (carrier or noncarrier)

intervention.value: Intravenous aducanumab, high dose or low dose, once every 4 weeks, with dose titration; high-dose target 10 mg/kg (titrated from 1 to 3 to 6 to 10 mg/kg over 24 weeks) from protocol version 4; low dose 3 mg/kg in ApoE ε4 carriers or 6 mg/kg in noncarriers
intervention.quote: Participants were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to high-dose or low-dose intravenous aducanumab or placebo once every 4 weeks. Dose titration was used as a risk-minimization strategy.

comparator.value: Placebo (n = 1087 in the safety population; n = 1076 in the MRI safety population)
comparator.quote: The placebo-controlled period of the combined EMERGE and ENGAGE trials included 2198 aducanumab-treated participants (2752 total person-years of exposure) and 1087 participants receiving placebo.

biomarker_confirmation.value: Amyloid pathology confirmed by visual assessment of amyloid positron emission tomography
biomarker_confirmation.quote: with amyloid pathology confirmed by visual assessment of amyloid positron emission tomography. See the eMethods in for the inclusion and exclusion criteria.

harms.name: Radiographic resolution of ARIA-E events
harms.quote: Of all ARIA-E events in the 10-mg/kg group, 479 (98.2%) were observed to have resolved (ie, no residual brain edema) during the study; specifically, 336 (68.9%) resolved within 12 weeks and 404 (82.8%) resolved within 16 weeks.

limitations: Potential limitations of this work include the early termination of the trials (35% of participants in the EMERGE trial and 30% in the ENGAGE trial withdrew owing to early study termination), which led to fewer patients completing a full course of dosing and could potentially impact the incidence of adverse events.
Additionally, the global phase 3 study populations lacked racial and ethnic diversity; therefore, very limited data about the frequency and severity of ARIA in diverse populations are available.

Data are not available for initiation of treatment at other stages of disease (ie, preclinical) or later (ie, moderate to severe dementia) stages of AD, and initiation of aducanumab is not indicated in those populations.

Important to the interpretation of ARIA-H incidence in this study is the fact that patients with preexisting microhemorrhages (more than 4) or areas of superficial siderosis were excluded from the phase 3 trials, which may have contributed to the overall observed incidence of ARIA-H.

More real-world data on the treatment and management of ARIA, outside of the clinical trial protocols, are required to assess which medications may be effective in treating symptomatic patients with ARIA.

risk_of_bias.judgement: The document acknowledges the potential for functional unblinding due to ARIA and states it was addressed in the study design by separating efficacy raters from safety raters and keeping efficacy raters blinded to ARIA assessments.
risk_of_bias.quote: The potential for functional unblinding due to ARIA is a consideration in studies of anti-Aβ antibodies, and it was considered in the study design.

risk_of_bias.judgement: 44.8% of the safety population did not complete the placebo-controlled period, predominantly because the sponsor terminated the studies early, which the document itself says could affect the incidence of adverse events.
risk_of_bias.quote: 1473 (44.8%) had not completed the period (EMERGE, n = 764; ENGAGE, n = 709), with the predominant reason being early study termination by the sponsor (EMERGE, 572 patients [35%]; ENGAGE, 491 [30%])

risk_of_bias.judgement: The analyses in this report were not in the trial protocol; most were prespecified only in the integrated summary of safety, which is not the protocol-level prespecification a reader might assume.
risk_of_bias.quote: The primary analysis will be reported elsewhere. Most of the secondary analyses for this report were prespecified for the integrated summary of safety but were not included in the trial protocol.

risk_of_bias.judgement: The document states that some analyses in this report are ad hoc analyses performed to address regulatory queries, so they are not prespecified.
risk_of_bias.quote: Some ad hoc analyses to address regulatory queries are of scientific interest and are therefore included as part of this report.

risk_of_bias.domain: selection — baseline exclusion of hemorrhage-prone participants
risk_of_bias.judgement: Participants with more than 4 baseline microhemorrhages or any siderosis were excluded, which the document states may have contributed to the observed ARIA-H incidence.
risk_of_bias.quote: Patients with more than 4 microhemorrhages or any area of siderosis on gradient echo MRI sequences at baseline were excluded.

risk_of_bias.judgement: Treatment groups in the pooled analysis are based on target dose in the randomized regimen, and the high-dose carrier target dose was changed mid-study from 6 mg/kg to 10 mg/kg in protocol version 4, so the 6-mg/kg group is a remainder group rather than a cleanly randomized comparator.
risk_of_bias.quote: For participants in the safety population randomized to the high-dose carrier group (n = 746), the target dose was changed from 6 mg/kg to 10 mg/kg in protocol version 4.

disagreements.question: Was the futility analysis that terminated EMERGE and ENGAGE valid?
disagreements.position: The document states that after termination it was determined that key assumptions underlying the futility decision were not valid, and that final data were collected per protocol and analyzed per the prespecified analysis plan.
disagreements.attributed_to: the authors of this report (Salloway et al, JAMA Neurology, sponsor-affiliated analysis of EMERGE and ENGAGE)
disagreements.quote: The EMERGE and ENGAGE trials were terminated early based on futility analysis. After termination, it was determined that key assumptions on which the futility decision was based were not valid.

disagreements.question: Is it acceptable to continue dosing through radiographically mild, asymptomatic ARIA-E?
disagreements.position: The document concludes continued dosing for asymptomatic and radiographically limited ARIA-E is feasible, because most such events did not increase in size or involve multiple brain locations and patients typically remained asymptomatic.
disagreements.attributed_to: the authors of this report (Salloway et al, JAMA Neurology)
disagreements.quote: the results indicate that continued dosing for asymptomatic and radiographically limited ARIA-E is feasible since, during uninterrupted dosing, most ARIA-E events did not increase in size or involve multiple brain locations and patients remained typically asymptomatic

disagreements.question: Which factors increase the risk of ARIA in aducanumab-treated patients?
disagreements.position: The document reports that only pretreatment brain microhemorrhages and ApoE ε4 carrier status were associated with increased incidence of ARIA-E, and that these same factors did not confer increased risk of ARIA-H; age, sex, AD stage and antithrombotic use showed no association with ARIA-E.
disagreements.attributed_to: the authors of this report (Salloway et al, JAMA Neurology)
disagreements.quote: Among other demographic and baseline characteristics, only pretreatment brain microhemorrhages and ApoE ε4 carrier status were found to be associated with an increase in the incidence of ARIA-E. These same factors did not confer an increased risk of ARIA-H.
